summary: The design fits existing linked-surface seams, but the main risks are server-side authorization identity, missing persistence context for ephemeral surfaces, and an underspecified transformer contract. The current registry and executor also do not yet provide the alias, output-shape, validation, error, or post-transform row-limit guarantees this feature requires.

suggestions.title: Put one-source execution behind LinkedSurfaceService
suggestions.rationale: LinkedSurfaceService currently owns guard enforcement, owner authorization, snapshot execution, and refresh error mapping. A handler-local call to execute_sources could bypass or duplicate those rules. Add a service-level fetch_source operation and have UISurfacesHandler only resolve surface access and serialize its result.

suggestions.title: Accept parameter overrides, not client-supplied query conditions
suggestions.rationale: The existing executor derives conditions from the persisted request, declared parameters, locked values, and the 5000-row cap. If the new endpoint accepts the renderer's raw conditions, a client can alter locked filters, tenant-related fields, or querylimit. Define the endpoint body as source parameter overrides and reconstruct conditions server-side from the persisted descriptor.

suggestions.title: Resolve viewer-versus-owner identity and share-token propagation explicitly
suggestions.rationale: Direct renderer fetches use the viewer JWT, while the existing server refresh deliberately uses the owner's PermissionContext. resolve_surface_access authorizes a surface but does not expose the access mode, and A2UISurface currently sends only the persisted id and bearer header. A shared viewer can therefore either fail to call the new endpoint or execute under an unintended identity. Define the pctx rule, preserve 404/403 semantics, and propagate the share token through the linked lane if share access is supported.

suggestions.title: Specify what happens when a Python-transform source is not persisted
suggestions.rationale: The proposed endpoint resolves a descriptor from a persisted surface, but persistedSurfaceId is optional and the current linked lane can render an in-memory envelope. Such a surface has no server-side record to resolve. Require persistence before enabling the Python member, or introduce a separately authenticated/signed descriptor flow; never silently fall back to direct QuerySource because that drops the transform.

suggestions.title: Align input_alias with the existing transformer registry contract
suggestions.rationale: Registered transformers currently expect different aliases such as snapshots or df, and validate_inputs checks manifest requirements using those aliases. Calling every function with the proposed default source alias will make existing built-ins fail with KeyError or skip their manifest requirements. Require an explicit compatible alias, or define a single-input adapter and validate it against the manifest before execution.

suggestions.title: Define the transformer result-to-rows contract
suggestions.rationale: The registry contract returns an arbitrary dict: existing transformers return scalars, nested objects, or a rows list. The linked executor and frame_to_records require a pandas DataFrame, while the existing multi-frame selector only operates on QuerySource results. Specify whether the selected value must be a list of row objects or a DataFrame, convert it through one shared helper, and reject scalar or ambiguous nested results deterministically.

suggestions.title: Separate transform-stage failures from data-stage failures
suggestions.rationale: execute_sources currently catches every exception and map_query_error maps generic ValueError, KeyError, and callable failures to 502 data_stage. That conflicts with the intended runtime 422 for unknown, unavailable, invalid-input, or failed transformers. Add a stable transform error type/code and map it independently in both the service and HTTP handler.

suggestions.title: Create a shared linked-transform validation gate
suggestions.rationale: The toolkit currently validates TransformSpec structure but does not check registry membership, manifest columns, or transformer parameters; validate_inputs only accepts recipe TransformStep and is not directly applicable to a linked source. Add a source-specific gate reusable by builder/probe, persistence, and runtime so registration failures are caught early and runtime revalidation remains fail-closed.

suggestions.title: Enforce row and serialization limits after transformation
suggestions.rationale: The existing 5000-row limit applies to the QuerySource fetch, while the 500-row limit is applied only when snapshotting. A Python transformer can expand or synthesize rows after the fetch, so the new endpoint could exceed the stated response bound. Apply an explicit post-transform row budget and the existing JSON-safe frame serialization before returning or persisting data.

suggestions.title: Update the Python schema source and regenerate UI types
suggestions.rationale: The UI types module re-exports generated declarations, and the committed schema/types are generated artifacts. The feature must update the Pydantic model, regenerate ui/schemas/LinkedSources.json and LinkedSources.d.ts, and extend the codegen drift tests; editing types.ts alone would leave the contract inconsistent.

suggestions.title: Add an end-to-end matrix for auth, transformer parity, and lane routing
suggestions.rationale: Current tests cover direct QuerySource URL selection, existing refresh identity, and ordinary executor transforms, but no per-source endpoint or Python-transform renderer branch exists. Add cases for owner/scope/share access, missing guard, wrong source key, locked-parameter tampering, viewer/owner pctx selection, unknown transformer, alias/output failures, 422 versus 502 mapping, row caps, and Python executor versus endpoint row equality.

suggestions.title: Consider a persisted/server-refresh-only first phase
suggestions.rationale: The repository already has a guarded owner-context Python execution path through ensure_snapshot and refresh. If dynamic browser execution cannot yet settle identity, share propagation, and ephemeral-surface handling, initially reject Python transforms in non-persisted renderer lanes and support them only during persistence/server refresh. This reduces the new HTTP and authorization surface, at the cost of not providing live client refresh for those sources.
